title: Epilogue
html:
Endings Game Over screens Epilogue

Six months after the resolution of ⁠Confront the Elder Brain, the party gathers for an extended Epilogue sequence, which takes place at a suppertime gathering thrown by  Withers at the Wilderness campsite. The gathering serves as an opportunity for all the companions to reunite and share how they have been faring since parting ways, as well as to gain closure on the stories of each companion. The epilogue was added in Patch 5.

The epilogue sequence is tailored to the decisions made throughout the preceding playthrough and, as such, contains many variations. Major changes pivot around choices made during Confront the Elder Brain and the resolutions of each companion's Personal Quests. In multiplayer games, all player characters in the party at the time of the Netherbrain's defeat attend the epilogue. Anyone who permanently died or otherwise left the party permanently during the playthrough cannot participate in the epilogue.

Location

The epilogue takes place at night in a unique instance of the Wilderness campsite. Tables and barrels overflowing with food and wine stretch across its east end, a bonfire burns in the centre, and festive banners and flowers decorate the rocks throughout.

 Potions of Animal Speaking can be found throughout, allowing the player character to  Speak with Animals if they do not naturally have the ability.[1]

Withers' workshop

The stone ruin in the southeast corner has been turned into a type of office for Withers. On the north wall lies a book-strewn desk topped with  Scroll of Disintegrate,  Scroll of Circle of Death, and  Volo's Guide to Baldur's Gate (Signed). An alchemical altar sits against the eastern wall, next to  The Book of Willing Souls. Lining the southern wall is his sarcophagus and an end table, upon which are two D20 dice named Divine Odds.[2] The bottle rack in the north-western corner contains a  Potion of Animal Speaking.

Bandstand

 Milil stands upon a central stone, surrounded by spiritual instruments, and provides music for the party. If passing a Religion check, Milil is identified as the erstwhile minor deity of song, a recognition which gives him great joy. Milil acts as a jukebox, changing the song per the player character's requests. The song options are:

  • Can you play a pretty song, reminiscent of taverns and tales? – Plays  Ale of Balduran
  • Something lively that encourages dancing would be perfect. – Plays  Bard Dance
  • How about something thoughtful, hopeful? – Plays  New Light
  • I'd like something that feels rich and warm. – Plays  Streets and Faces
  • Something nostalgic and gentle would be ideal. – Plays  We Live Another Day
  • Do you have any new compositions? Something that's never been heard before? – Plays  Endless Spring (a new song specific to the epilogue)

Companions will remark nostalgically about being back at the campsite through conversation and ambient banter.

Clothing Chest

A  Clothing Chest at X: -511 Y: -498contains a vast number of dyes, camp clothes, shoes, and undergarments, allowing the player character to customise their outfit.

Chest of Grateful Words & Gazette bulletin board

The  Chest of Grateful Words and multiple editions of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette can be found at X: -481 Y: -504. Here, it is possible to quickly catch up on the developments of some characters, who either send correspondence which can be found in the chest's inventory or make headlines on the posted editions of the Gazette. The headlines of the Gazette are modular, with some headlines being constant and others being affected by outcomes from the playthrough.[verify] For example:

  • Contains an update on Alfira and a consequence from not completing Free the Artist, among others.
  • Contains fallout from sinking the Iron Throne, among others
  • Contains update on Duke Ravengard and Wulbren Bongle, among others.
  • Contains updates on Rolan and Minsc, among others.

Attendees

Origin Character

The primary player character's behaviour in the epilogue will differ significantly depending on the chosen Origin. The behaviour is also influenced by the party member(s) romanced and whether the player character became a Mind Flayer.

Illithid Transformation

Player characters who opted for the complete mind flayer transformation remain in their illithid form, and the other attendees remark on their appearance, but are happy to see them nonetheless. Like a non-illithid origin character, player characters still have the option to hug  Gale,  Shadowheart,  Karlach,  Halsin, and  Minsc, as well as embrace or kiss their romantic partner(s) as a mind flayer.

However, each time they speak to a companion, it becomes increasingly likely the player character will be struck with the compulsion to eat their brain[3]. A  DC 15 Constitution Check is required to resist[4]; if failing or voluntarily giving in, the companion becomes hostile, and Withers unceremoniously whisks the player character through a portal.

In fact, the mind flayer player character turns out to be quite a gourmand while considering the palatability of their former companions' brains and sometimes even demonstrates a certain measure of humour:

  • About Astarion: "Astarion's sweet brain may be a bit less wrinkled than the rest, but you hunger for its teasing cells. His parietal lobe - which controls his sense of touch - will be an aphrodisiac in your maw."
  • About Gale: "You would save his temporal lobe for last, if you were to eat Gale. Language. Learning. Memory. He must have quite a fine example."
  • About Halsin: "Every time Halsin speaks of balance, your thoughts cannot behave. You only think of what cerebellum tastes like when it sends the signals to his vestibular system to keep him from wobbling."
  • About Jaheira: "Weary Jaheira. Over time, her stresses may have shrunk her hippocampus, making its taste more intense."
  • About Karlach: "You consider Karlach's brain stem - the stalk meant to regulate her body's temperature. Will it come pre-cooked?"
  • About Lae'zel: "Lae'zel's motor cortex - that which controls her fine movements - will be harshly disciplined. That will make her especially chewy - just how you like a cortex to be."
  • About Minsc: "There are cruel rumours spread, that Minsc may once have suffered injury to his brain. You could set the slander right at last - tell the world every bite was perfect."
  • About Minthara: "With all Minthara's hate, you wonder if her cerebro-spinal fluid will be bitter to sip."
  • About Shadowheart: "Think of Shadowheart's cerebellum, which controls her dextrous hands. Any ritual caster must have a tightly commanded hindbrain."
  • About Wyll: "Wyll's frontal lobe, which processes his judgement and measured words, would be a delicacy befitting his nobility."

Dark Urge

The appearance of the Dark Urge in the epilogue varies depending on whether the Urge was embraced or rejected. The party plays out normally if the Urge was rejected, though talking to  Astarion in his spawn ending has him secretly pull out a dagger and ask if they have fully overcome their bloodlust before putting it away when they confirm this. If the Urge was embraced, however, the player character cannot interact with the party. Instead, a blood-soaked player character stumbles into the campsite from afar with insanity in their eyes, as  Bhaal has lived up to his promise to shred their mind if they did not take over the Netherbrain. They contemplate killing all the other attendees in their sleep while licking  Bloodthirst.

Companions

Astarion

 Astarion's appearance and behaviour at the party are determined primarily by the outcome of ⁠The Pale Elf and ⁠Investigate Cazador's Palace, namely, whether or not he ascended after  Cazador Szarr's death and whether or not he made amends with the Gur tribe in Rivington.

Vampire Spawn

If Astarion neither finished his companion quest nor spoke to the Gur in Act Three, he goes into hiding, unable to walk in the sun or on the streets in fear that Cazador might find him. He shares that he has returned to eating vermin and asks the player character to help him kill Cazador. If the player character agrees, Astarion responds that this means a great deal to him, and they can set off in the morning. If the player character refuses, Astarion remarks that he has always been alone and should not have expected this to change.

If Astarion did not confront Cazador but did reconcile with the Gur, he shares that they killed Cazador without much effort after tearing out his tongue. He says he has embraced living in the shadows, but he would like to live in the sun if an opportunity presents itself.

If Astarion was convinced not to ascend, he shows up in a neutral-colored doublet and acts like his usual self: flamboyant, energetic, and happy to be killing; however, he is now an adventuring vigilante, only killing people who deserve it. He has grown acclimated to living in darkness, developing a renewed sense of self and accepting his own identity and nature, which inspires hope in people. If the player character romanced Astarion and encouraged him to find a way to walk in the sun, he says he has been searching the world for one.

If the player character romanced Astarion, spared the spawn, and proposed they lead the spawn together in the Underdark, Astarion shares that they have built a vampire haven from some abandoned ruins, Szarr Palace has been burned down, and all knowledge of the Rite of Profane Ascension has been lost.

Ambient chatter from Astarion in any outcome where he is a spawn has him bemoan that Withers has brought fine wine from all over the world but has not thought to bring any fresh blood. He goes on to try the reddest wines available, but none are blood.

Vampire Ascendant

If Astarion ascended, he shows up wearing an opulent blood-red suit and speaks more slowly, with a venomous drip. He brags about his rising status as the city's "puppet master" and generally looks down upon the player character. If Wyll has also become a Grand Duke, Astarion bemoans the difficulties he faces trying to bypass him. He can be challenged on his new behaviour and compared to Cazador, but Astarion brushes these accusations off. Unlike other companions, the entire camp always sides with the player character if Astarion ascended and they (as an illithid) attempt to eat his brain, but Withers still triggers the bad ending after the fight.

If the player character romanced Astarion and remained with him as his spawn (or ally in the case of illithid transformation), he asks them to talk with the other companions, gather information, and share any secrets with him later, while he stays behind and drinks wine. He is surprised to hear the others are somehow achieving successes in life without his supervision, but he is not interested enough to engage in conversation with them himself. If spoken with again, he tells the player character they have an eternity for chatting.

Ambient chatter from Astarion as a vampire lord has him admit (albeit reluctantly) how nice the party is, admire himself in a hand mirror, react to all the wines brought by Withers, or turn into bat form and try but fail to eavesdrop on other conversations.

Gale

 Gale's presence and behaviour at the party are determined primarily by the outcome of ⁠The Wizard of Waterdeep, namely whether he gave up the Crown of Karsus to  Mystra, kept the Crown for himself to become a god, or sacrificed himself to destroy the  Netherbrain.

Professor

If he survived but did not keep the Crown, Gale returns to Waterdeep with  Tara as a professor at the Blackstaff Academy's School of Illusion. If he chose to return the Crown to Mystra, she cures him of his Netherese Orb; otherwise, if he left it hidden in the ocean, Mystra leaves the orb as a reminder of his former hubris but deactivates it so he can live in peace. He pretends the orb is still active in order to threaten his students and keep control of the classroom.

He asks the player character to come by the school at some point as a guest lecturer for his class. Player characters can accept (with or without their romantic partner), with the particular line depending on their Class, or gently decline. Illithid characters can express doubt on the students willing to listen to them, or express fear of exposion of their true form. If the lecture proposition is declined, Gale asks simply to visit him, promising to provide a fine wine (or a special "cerebral" diet for a ceremorphed friend). In either version of the professor ending, Gale can be hugged during the player character's first conversation with him.

If the player character romanced Gale without giving him the Crown, the two arrive together as newlyweds. Gale is concerned about his appearance, but thanks the player character for encouraging him to come to the party. If they stayed in Waterdeep, he asks the player character about their opinion of the city and remarks how much has changed since the party first met and how much he has missed everyone. If the couple stayed in Baldur's Gate, they can discuss their participation in rebuilding the city, particularly Gale's magical help in strengthening the High Hall constructions. Either case, Gale then sends the player character off so he is not tempted to keep them to himself all night, but he can be kissed goodbye first.

Gale's ambient chatter as a human mostly consists of discussing with Tara other companions or the best corners of the realm.

God of Ambition

If Gale decided to take the Crown for himself, he arrives at the party after having become the god of ambition. He shares that he reforged the Crown and used it to ascend to godhood, but left Mystra to her magical domain. He has several temples already built in his honour, and he promises that the player character is never out of his sight.

Ambient chatter of a god Gale has him comparing the material plane to Elysium. From time to time he conjures a glass of wine, instead of choosing something from the feast table. He is also talking haughtily to  Tara, who is unhappy with Gale's ascension, though, calling his change "distasteful".

If the player character romanced Gale, he invites them to join him in  Elysium, promising them they would eventually find their own purpose as a deity.

Spectral Voice

If he used the Netherese Orb to destroy the Netherbrain, a magical projection of Gale called the Spectral Voice attends the party in his stead. This projection informs the player character it was created by Gale in the event that he died and was beyond normal means of resurrection. It then passes on an  Improvised Letter containing a farewell message. If the player character romanced Gale while he was alive, they can attempt (but fail) to kiss the projection goodbye, and it remarks it can see why Gale loved them so much. The Spectral Voice then vanishes, and Tara is saddened by his death.

Halsin

 Halsin does not have any significant changes to his behaviour or appearance at the party, but his dialogue differs based on whether the player character is partnered with him and, if so, whether they returned to Thaniel's realm with him in his romance wrap-up scene.

Reithwin Town

If the player character has both romanced Halsin and moved in with him, he expresses concern about this being their first night away from Reithwin Town and asks if they regret choosing their quiet new life over adventuring. If the player character talks to him a second time, he practices several bear puns on the player character but apologises for the children's sense of humour rubbing off on him.

Otherwise, after optionally sharing a hug (and a kiss if romanced), he talks of settling down in Reithwin Town and asks for a story from the player character to bring back to his hordes of newly adopted children. The player character can joke with Halsin that they would have asked him to read them stories and tuck them in during their adventure, and if they romanced him, they can also tease him that some stories will have to wait until the children are older. If the player character went to Avernus with  Karlach, Halsin says he is glad the player character's relationship with her has endured and can be used as a lesson for the children, but (if romanced) his heart will always be open to them when they get back. Before the player character leaves their first conversation, Halsin gives them a  Whittled Duck as a symbol of his joy to be back in their company, just as a duck returns home after migrating. It is also possible to ask him to take in the Owlbear, which he happily accepts.

Ambient chatter from Halsin, regardless of whether the player character stayed with him, shows he is surprised Withers brought so much food when he is mostly made of bone; he theorises that Withers is living vicariously through everyone else's appetites. He also says he should exercise restraint with the alcohol, lest he lose his faculties and ruin the party's atmosphere as a Wildshaped bear. He is thrilled to be among old friends and in nature. Throughout the party, Halsin can be seen dancing to Milil's music, and he occasionally becomes  Drunk, living up to his own worries by gorging on fruit or stumbling around as a bear until the condition wears off.

Jaheira

 Jaheira's behaviour at the dinner party is slightly different based on whether  Minsc was convinced to rely on her or not. The latter prompts her retirement.

In both of her endings, Jaheira talks of Baldur's Gate's reconstruction efforts and the roles which her children, the Harpers, and Minsc have to play in it. She reveals Jord has joined the Harpers and is planning crop cycles in Wyrm's Crossing. Rion has temporarily joined the Flaming Fist, but she mostly spends her time incarcerating corrupt Fists. The player character can ask her if they can join the Harpers, and she agrees, even if they are a mind flayer. Otherwise, she asks the player character what "home" means to them, and they can answer with either Baldur's Gate, the campsite, Karlach (if they went to Avernus with her), their romantic partner, or nowhere because they prefer adventuring. She then dismisses herself to make sure no one tampers with the drinks.

Jaheira has no ambient chatter during the party, but she can be seen practising the flute or swaying and tapping along to Milil's music.

High Harper

If she remained the High Harper, Jaheira mentions she has to house people and rebuild the Harper network. She also says she has little love for Baldur's Gate but chooses to serve the city for her family.

Retiree

If Minsc was convinced to be independent of her, Jaheira retires from the Harpers and settles down in Elerrathin's Home as a stay-at-home mother. She shares that she has done much more sitting down than she would like. She has also been heavily involved in her children's lives, and they have proven themselves capable of restoring the city on their own. Jaheira confesses that she misses adventuring and Baldur's Gate is, in fact, her home, but she remarks that one only realizes someplace is home after having left and looking back to it. Talking to her a second time has her promise to stop writing so many letters back to the city, much to the player character's disbelief.

Karlach

 Karlach's behaviour is determined primarily by the decisions made on the dock after defeating the Netherbrain and whether she became an illithid or not.

Avernus

If she went to Avernus, Karlach's dialogue varies slightly based on whether Wyll, the player character, or both accompanied her and whether she was romanced. Regardless, she is excited to have discovered a lead on permanently fixing her soul engine: blueprints for one of  Zariel's secret forges. Her ambient chatter in this ending has her comment on how good it smells and how beautiful it is at the campsite.

Illithid

If Karlach became a mind flayer, she appears as she did in the final battle. She talks slowly and airily, reporting that she still feels like herself, but eating brains has enriched her with lifetimes of additional thoughts and memories. She sustains herself through an arrangement with a healer for terminally ill patients, who consent to donate their brains to her diet, and she is proud of how their memories can live on through her.

Ambient chatter from Karlach as an illithid has her note that the reunion is a lovely occasion, but she soon gets hungry. She expresses pity that mutton chops no longer interest or sustain her and reminds herself not to think about any of the local brains, lest she tempt herself.

Death

If she did not go to Avernus or become an illithid, Karlach is dead and thus cannot show up. A conversation with Withers reveals she was not resurrected because she did not want to return, but he comforts the player character by sharing that her soul in the Fugue Plane is so bright that even the gods are blinded by it. If Shadowheart is alive and Minsc is working with  Nine-Fingers Keene, they both lament on Karlach's absence, but Minsc promises to make sure the Guild honours her memory.

Lae'zel

 Lae'zel's behaviour depends on the outcome of ⁠The Githyanki Warrior, namely whether she rejected or embraced  Vlaakith; whether  Orpheus was freed or assimilated; and whether she flew back to the Astral Plane to wage war against Vlaakith or stayed in Faerûn.

If the  Githyanki Egg was left in Lae'zel's possession, she speaks of the young man born of it, named Xan ("freedom" in Gith), in the care of allies. She also speaks of what kind of adventurer her adoptive son has become.

Ascension

If she remained loyal to Vlaakith and accepted ascension, Lae'zel has died and thus cannot show up. When spoken to, Withers explains that githyanki ascension means being consumed by Vlaakith, and he can no longer sense Lae'zel's presence.

Limbo

If Lae'zel sides with Orpheus and departs with him to wage war (or goes alone if he became a mind flayer), she appears at the party as a glowing  Astral Projection, supporting which requires efforts of a dozen gishes, or Orpheus alone. She explains this as being on a diplomatic mission to the Githzerai, recounts tales of victory, and mentions her new appreciation for things other than battle.

If the player character romanced Lae'zel and agreed to leave with her to the Astral Plane, they both appear as projections, and all other companions mention this while talking to them.

In this ending, Xan is currently staying with the mages of Xamvadi'm.

Ambient chatter from Lae'zel as an Astral Projection has her relieved that her projection is holding. She is glad to see Faerûn's skies again, having learned much during the adventure. She is especially pleased with the camaraderie and revelry happening on the eve of her victory against Vlaakith.

Faerûn

If Lae'zel sided with Orpheus but decided to stay in Faerûn, she launches a crusade to slay every Vlaakith-aligned Githyanki on the  Sword Coast, and she invites the player character to join her in rooting out the last major stronghold in  Chult.[5]

Minsc

 Minsc's appearance and dialogue at the party depend on the outcome of ⁠Aid the Underduke and the subsequent conversation with  Nine-Fingers Keene.

Ambient chatter from Minsc in either ending has him being impressed with the quality of meat Withers provided, though neither he nor  Boo knows where Withers sourced it. The player character can also hug Minsc, who notes that Boo shed fur on them during the hug and thus will always be with them.

Zhentarim Prisoner

If Minsc was not present for the conversation with Nine-Fingers Keene, he refused to make amends with her, or the player character sided with the Zhentarim, he arrives looking worse for wear, decked in rags. Without knowing the gravity of his situation, he reveals he was kidnapped by the Zhentarim and was about to be executed until Withers rescued him by spiriting him away to the party.

Berserker Lodge

If Minsc agreed to help the Guild as their "berserker lodge", he appears well-dressed and accompanied by  Happy Hoarson, a halfling from the Guild, whom he was in the middle of terrorizing for looting corpses. Minsc commends the player character and their companions for being ideal heroic role models, the kind of people Happy should strive to be more like. He also comments on how he no longer sleeps in "that" sewer, instead having found a much nicer sewer to sleep in.

An additional line of ambient chatter from Minsc in this ending has him exclaim to Boo that Happy must be treated nicely if he is to reform.

Minthara

 Minthara's appearance and behaviour at the party depends on whether the player character encourages her to stay in Baldur's Gate.

When spoken to in either ending, Minthara bemoans the party's lack of extravagance, comparing it with the celebrations she had participated in as a member of her House in Menzoberranzan. Still, she says that those parties, unlike the current one, were for the most part merely another way of scheming and assassination attempts. She also asks if the player character regrets their decision not to control the Absolute. In any case, she is eager to leave as soon as possible.

If the player character is romancing Minthara, she talks of a fine opportunity to poison the feast. One of possible options to reply (though not leading to any consequences) is to suggest her spiking the drinks, while the player character manages the food.

Ambient chatter from Minthara has her wryly suspect there have been other reunions to which she has not been invited, worry that all the heroes gathering together paints a target on the party for attacks, and relate that she is becoming accustomed to the taste of surface-grown plants.

Menzoberranzan

If Minthara did not stay in Baldur's Gate, she reveals she has returned to  Menzoberranzan in the Underdark, despite being an apostate of  Lolth. She is now gathering like-minded individuals to reclaim her family house and wage war on the Spider-Queen.

Baldur's Gate

Otherwise, Minthara proclaims that Baldur's Gate needs new leadership, which she is happy to provide. She shares how she has been scheming in the shadows, and says the political intrigue has been enjoyable. She says the people will learn from her or bow to her.

Shadowheart

 Shadowheart's behaviour is determined by the outcome of ⁠Daughter of Darkness, whether she rejected or embraced  Shar and whether her parents are alive or not. When the player character talks to Shadowheart for the first time, she automatically hugs them (the only companion to do so) before commenting on the player character's improved physique.

Ambient chatter from Shadowheart in any ending has her being pleased at the quality of wine Withers brought for the party before promptly wondering why the party had to scavenge food from barrels and crates during their adventure when Withers could have fed them. She then recalls a night where fourteen apples, some fish heads, and stale bread were served for dinner. This line can be heard regardless of which camp supplies were used during the adventure.

Mother Superior

If she became the Mother Superior, she mentions how the rebuilding of Baldur's Gate is all-consuming but has led to many new recruits for Shar's following.

Adventurer

If Shadowheart rejected Shar but let her parents die, she embarks on a life of adventuring and slaying Sharran assassins, telling the player character of visiting the  House of the Moon in  Waterdeep. If the player character romanced her and joined her adventures, she also recounts when the couple befriended an Imp named Bing Bong. If the player character married Gale, they can call her out for not visiting them while venturing to the temple, but she admits she did not want to rope them in if a Sharran was hunting her and promises to visit Waterdeep again once it is safer. If the player character went to Avernus with Karlach (and possibly Wyll), she expresses interest in joining them on their adventures once Karlach is finally able to return to Faerûn. If asked about her parents, she says she still feels their presence in moonmotes and looks forward to reuniting with them when she dies.

Farmer

If Shadowheart both rejected Shar and saved her parents, she has moved into a rustic cottage with her parents and an abundance of pets, one of which is an orphan wolf cub, thus revealing she has overcome her fear of wolves.[6] If the player character has her take in the Armoured Owlbear, she can be pressured to make room for him in her cow's barn or even renovate her bedroom so she can have him as her bunkmate.

Talking to Shadowheart a second time in either ending where she rejected Shar has her share how she has been making hard ciders with apples of her own, but she is bored of doing it alone. The player character can suggest she start a cider brewery or learn to juggle. Talking to her a third time has her express her gratitude to Withers for watching over everyone's souls and keeping them alive for so long.

Wyll

 Wyll's behaviour is determined by the outcome of ⁠The Blade of Frontiers, namely whether he was transformed into a devil or not, whether he became a Duke or not, and whether he remained a Warlock or escaped his contract. If freed of his contract, he arrives as a Level 12 Ranger of the Hunter subclass, regardless of what level or class(es) he had during the events of the game.

Ambient chatter from Wyll in any ending has him enjoying the music, company, wine, and especially fresh air. He wishes the night could last forever. He can also occasionally be seen dancing to Milil's music with similar moves to his Act Two romance scene.

Blade of Frontiers

If Wyll never completed his personal quest or he killed Karlach but declined becoming Grand Duke, he simply remains the Blade of Frontiers, still becoming a ranger if he broke his contract. He tells the player character about slaying a stegosaurus in  Candlekeep that was accidentally enlarged by a wizard, an "impossible lich" he ran into while camping, or a son of the dragon  Claugiyliamatar who had terrorised an enclave of elves.

Grand Duke

If he became a Grand Duke in the city, he arrives at the party in splendid finery and tells the player character of his acclimation to the political intrigue of Baldur's Gate; he also reveals the Council of Four has been disbanded. If  Ulder Ravengard survived, his new title is Grand Duke of the Triad, Keeper of the Fist. If Ulder Ravengard died,  Liara Portyr has become the Grand Duke of the Wilds, Sickle of Chult. If  Florrick survived, she has become Grand Duke of the Crossing, The Face of Devotion. If Florrick died and  Cordula Eltan lives, she has become the Grand Duke of the  Seatower, a Legacy Reborn. Wyll's official title is Grand Duke of the Wyrm, Heart of the Gate. If the player character romanced Wyll, he offers to nominate them as Grand Duke of the Coast, Doom of the Dead Three.

If left to serve his contract, he says  Mizora is helping him rebuild the city, but he does not understand what she is planning.

Blade of Avernus

If Wyll was transformed by Mizora and chose not to become the Grand Duke, he becomes the Blade of Avernus; he arrives smelling of sulfur and dressed in spiky armour, which he claims was made from the shattered bones of slain fiends.

If he broke his contract but Karlach chose to die, he travels to Avernus alone and shares that he has a lead on getting closer to claiming his revenge on Mizora.

If the player character romanced Wyll and chose to help him hunt Mizora, the couple recollects fights against enemies such as an  Amnizu, a pack of  Goristroi, and an  Orthon with three tusks. They also recall a visit to a diabolist who has a lead on reverse engineering Wyll's sending stone eye, which will allow him to track Mizora instead of vice versa. Wyll praises the player character for their heroism, saying that while devils fear their name, the Sword Coast praises it.

If Karlach died and Wyll continued to serve his contract, he reports that he still undertakes missions on Mizora's behalf, and his next quest has him tasked to slay a certain very powerful devil, though he cannot say more.

If Wyll moved to Avernus with Karlach (and the player character if chosen), he notes how many cambions the two (or three) of them have slain and expresses his hope for Karlach to get her engine fixed and return to Faerûn for good. If he kept his contract with Mizora, he reveals she has allowed him much more freedom as the Blade of Avernus, to his own surprise; he still mentions his next task of slaying a devil, but he is not afraid when Karlach or the player character have his back. If his contract was severed, he says he hopes to use Zariel's private forge to reverse engineer his stone eye so he can track Mizora and get his revenge on her later.

In all Blade of Avernus endings where Duke Ravengard is alive, Wyll also shares that he visits his father often and talks about his father's efforts to rebuild the corrupted Flaming Fist; he expresses how both he and his father are proud of each other.

Camp Followers

Owlbear Cub

The  Owlbear Cub's appearance and dialogue differ slightly depending on whether the player character ⁠cleared the Goblin Camp, saved  Isobel from  Marcus, and kept  Dammon alive to upgrade him into an ally against the Netherbrain.

Armoured Owlbear

If the cub both became the fully grown Armoured Owlbear and survived the final battle, he shows up with the same appearance. He can be pet by the player character and told they are glad he came, to which he becomes flustered. Asking what he has been up to with  Speak with Animals active has him share that he befriended a turtle, a cat, and a kraken, but he killed the kraken after it ate the cat. Talking to him without Speak with Animals shows him attempting to mimic his fight with the kraken, but he is mistaken for dancing.

Juvenile Cub

If the cub survived the events of the story but was not upgraded by Dammon, he still naturally grows up to a similar size on his own, but he lacks the enhanced strength or armour of his fully grown counterpart. He shares a similar story of befriending the same creatures, but since he was not strong enough to face the kraken, he was forced to run away in shame.

In either ending, the cub also reveals to Speak with Animals casters that he was never actually invited, instead following the player character's pleasant smell to join the party. It is possible to let him move in with either Halsin, Shadowheart (if she rejected Shar), or the player character (if partnered with one or both of them); both he and the corresponding companion are delighted by any choice.

Scratch

 Scratch appears very much his old self, but his petting dialogue option changes to "Pet your old friend Scratch", he makes new purr-like noises while being pet, and he asks to play fetch with the  Inert Astral Prism. If the player character uses  Speak with Animals, he shares that he stayed in Baldur's Gate after the group parted ways and became best friends with a young girl named Mindy. The player character can tell Scratch they are glad he is doing well, and he responds that he believes they both always will. After talking to Scratch once, the player character can find the Astral Prism on the ground,[7] and throwing it allows them to play fetch with him as he requested.

Volo

 Volo attends the party, sharing with the player character how he has an upcoming book about the party's adventures. He is shameless about forging the player character's signature in order to get his book made.

Withers

 Withers remains in his private chapel away from the celebration. Talking to him and selecting "I think I've caught up with everyone. What comes next?" triggers the good ending of the epilogue, in which Withers gives a speech wishing the companions a life of love and well-being. The player character can then give a toast of their choice, ending the epilogue and triggering the credits.

Other Attendees

Happy Hoarson

 Happy Hoarson is a Guild member brought to the party by Minsc if the latter made amends with Nine-Fingers Keene. When spoken to, he expresses concern that Boo might kill him.

Tara

 Tara participates in the party in all endings, wanting to meet the heroes with whom Gale saved Baldur's Gate. If he ascended to godhood, she remarks about how much she hates the change and invites the player character to meet his mother so the latter can hear about her son from someone who knew who he was before his ascension.

If Gale did not ascend to godhood, Tara invites the player character to come visit her and Gale and mentions that she will send the invitation by pigeon, remarking how she once had a taste for them.

If the player character romanced Gale and accepted his marriage proposal, Tara commends them for keeping him busier than he has ever been, but admits she misses seeing him as much. The player character can either invite her over for tea after the party, reassure her that she is still part of their new life, or simply tell her to get over it; however, if the latter is chosen, she declares they have made an enemy of her and will hiss whenever she is spoken to again. They can otherwise gossip about how messy Gale's study is before Tara shoos the player character away to the party, telling them they have earned it.

Raphael

 Raphael crashes the party if the player character signed his contract and gave the Crown of Karsus to him instead of Mystra. He also appears if Gale used the Crown to ascend to godhood, but since he is driven by ambition, which is Gale's domain, the latter can spirit him back to the House of Hope, destroying his pride and preventing him from getting the Crown altogether. Gale then says he needs to leave and prepare for the possibility of Raphael stealing it, but if the player character romanced him, he offers for them to join him and obtain the Crown's power as well.

Bad Ending

If the player character ruins the vibe by killing an attendee or attempting to eat someone's brain as a mind flayer, Withers unceremoniously bounces them from the party by sucking them through a portal; this immediately ends the epilogue and triggers the end credits. The player character can also damage and kill Withers himself for the first and only time in the game, but he simply reforms and bounces the player character anyway.
